CF Industries **+15.0% on the month, +2.3% Friday to $121.42** — the purest Iran trade on the board and still the highest-beta name to a Hormuz resolution. Mechanism unchanged: Hormuz carries ~35% of traded urea; Middle East FOB urea is elevated; US producers run on cheap domestic gas (Henry Hub -10.1% 1M) and capture the spread. **BUT the nitrogen thesis needs qualifying — see fertilizer-urea: the urea benchmark has DE-ESCALATED ~50% from April on CHINESE export quotas reopening, not on anything Iranian. CF's equity is running on the Middle East FOB spread and cheap US gas, not on a tightening global urea balance.** That makes the position more fragile than the +15% suggests. Yara's $1.3bn acquisition of Gulf Coast Ammonia, Texas City (2 Jul) is the corporate tell in the same direction: capital relocating ammonia capacity to cheap, secure US gas. CONFIRMED.

**+16.7% on the month to $123.57, +1.8% Monday** — but the attribution has now been corrected twice and should be read narrowly. **The move is a gas/ammonia MARGIN story — cheap US Henry Hub at -11.1% on the month against elevated Middle East FOB — not a Hormuz-tightness story.** The 19 July correction stands: **urea de-escalated ~50% from April on CHINESE export quotas reopening, not on anything Iranian**, with India's June tender clearing ~$445/t CFR against ~$890/t in April, heavily oversubscribed. **Phosphate, not nitrogen, is the tight leg** — DAP into India $920-935/t CFR, the highest since mid-2022. **That makes the CF position more fragile than +16.7% suggests: it is long a margin, not long a shortage.** ⚠️ No international urea/DAP/potash CFR print newer than the baseline could be obtained this cycle — flagged STALE.
